subject.title: Remote skill bin probe times out when node is co-located with gateway (macOS app as node on same host)

question: For macOS app-backed nodes that advertise `system.which` or `system.run`, should the gateway keep probing remote skill bins immediately on connect, or should it defer/back off/skip until an explicit readiness or host-capability signal is present?
rationale: The code can be fixed several plausible ways, but each changes user-visible remote skill availability, startup latency, and the security-sensitive boundary between app nodes and host-command nodes.

options.title: Require readiness-aware probe policy
options.body: Keep macOS app node command support, but defer the first bin probe until connectivity/readiness is proven and add bounded backoff after failed probes, with live co-located and remote-node proof.

options.title: Split app and host capabilities
options.body: Make app-backed nodes omit host-command capability until the app can actually service the probe path, leaving CLI/node-host sessions as the immediate probe targets.

options.title: Add an operator opt-out
options.body: Add a config flag only if maintainers decide users need a manual escape hatch after the default readiness behavior is fixed.

recommendation.title: Require readiness-aware probe policy
recommendation.body: Keep macOS app node command support, but defer the first bin probe until connectivity/readiness is proven and add bounded backoff after failed probes, with live co-located and remote-node proof.
